title: The checklist
blurb: Before every move, ask three questions: any checks, any captures, any attacks? Learn the habit that stops you hanging pieces and starts you finding tactics.
deeperTitle: Discovered attacks and checks; danger levels

core.title: Checks, captures, attacks
body: Before you move, ask three quick questions: any **checks**? Any **captures**? Any **attacks**? Look at yours first, then at your opponent's.
These are the forcing moves. They leave the other side few replies, so you can see what happens next.

board.caption: An attack: the knight and the bishop both aim at f7.

core.prompt: Checks come first. Tap a square where your knight can give check.
core.explain: From **e7** or **f6** the knight attacks the king on g8. Always list every check you have, even the ones that look odd. Sometimes one of them wins.

core.prompt: White to move. Find the check that leads to checkmate in two.
core.hint: You have several checks. Which one leaves Black only one legal reply?
core.explain: **Qc8+** leaves Black one reply: the bishop must block on d8, because the king has no square. Then **Qxd8#** is checkmate. None of your other checks forces mate. Your queen is attacked by the bishop on e5, but with a check every move Black never gets to take it.

core.prompt: Now captures. Before you take anything, ask which pieces are not protected. Tap a black piece that nothing protects.
core.explain: Nothing protects the knight on **e5**, or the pawn on a7. A piece that nothing protects can be taken for free, so look for one before you capture.

core.prompt: Several pieces can be taken here, but only one capture wins material. Find it.
core.hint: Before you take anything, ask: is it protected? One black piece is not.
core.explain: **dxe5** wins a knight that nothing protects, and the pawn now attacks the knight on f6 as well. **Bxh7+** looks tempting, but the knight on f6 simply takes the bishop.

core.prompt: Now an attack. You have no checks here. Find the quiet move that forces checkmate in two.
core.hint: Your bishop on h6 and your queen can both attack g7. Where should the queen go?
core.explain: **Qg5** threatens **Qxg7#**. Black cannot take the bishop with the g7 pawn, because that pawn is pinned to the king by your queen. Whatever Black plays, the mate cannot be stopped.

core.title: Now do it for your opponent
body: Then run the same three questions for the other side. If it were their move, what check, capture or attack would they play?
If the answer is dangerous, deal with it first.

board.caption: White to move. What would Black do with the move?

core.prompt: If it were Black's move, the queen would give checkmate. Tap the square.
core.explain: **Qxh2#**. The knight on g4 protects the queen, and your king has no square to run to. You found Black's threat by asking the checklist for the other side.

core.prompt: Now stop it. Make a move after which Black has no checkmate.
core.hint: You can block the queen's diagonal, or give your king a square to run to.
core.explain: **f4**, **g3** and **Bf4** all block the diagonal. **Re1** gives the king the f1 square. A move like **h3** does not help: the queen still takes on h2 with the knight's support.

core.title: Checks first
core.intro: List your checks, then pick the one that leaves Black the fewest replies. Each of these is checkmate in two.

puzzles.hint: A queen check on the back rank. Where can Black block?
puzzles.explain: **Qa8+** forces the bishop to block on e8, and **Qxe8#** takes it with checkmate.

puzzles.hint: Take with check. Where does the king have to go?
puzzles.explain: **Qxf7+** drives the king to h8. Then **Qxg7#** is checkmate, because the bishop on c3 protects the queen.

puzzles.hint: You are Black. Check on the back rank, and see what the knight must do.
puzzles.explain: **Qd1+** forces the knight to block on e1, and **Qxe1#** is checkmate.

core.title: Checklist for Black
core.intro: The same habit from Black's side. The board is flipped, so take your time. One quiet attack, one capture.

puzzles.hint: No check is needed. Aim at the weak pawn next to the king.
puzzles.explain: **Qg4** threatens **Qxg2#**, and the g2 pawn is pinned to the king, so White cannot take the bishop on h3 with it. The mate cannot be stopped.

puzzles.hint: One white piece is not protected by anything.
puzzles.explain: **dxe4** wins a knight for free, and the pawn attacks the knight on f3 as well.

deeper.title: The hidden attacker
body: A **discovered attack** happens when you move a piece out of the way and a piece behind it suddenly attacks. One move, two threats: the piece that moved, and the one it uncovered.

board.caption: The rook looks at the queen through its own knight.

deeper.prompt: Move the knight with check, and win the queen.
deeper.hint: Which knight move gives check? Then look at what the rook behind it can do.
deeper.explain: **Nf6+** is check, and it also uncovers the rook's attack on the queen. Black has to answer the check, so the queen cannot move. Next move the rook takes her.

deeper.prompt: Your bishop is in front of your rook. Move it with check and win the queen.
deeper.hint: The bishop can give check on the h7 square. What does that uncover?
deeper.explain: **Bh7+** is protected by the rook on h5, so the king cannot take it. The check uses up Black's turn, and the rook on d1 now takes the queen.

deeper.prompt: Why is a discovered check so strong?
options: The moved piece can make its own threat while Black must answer the check
A king in check cannot capture anything
deeper.explain: Black has to deal with the check, which uses their move. Meanwhile your moved piece can do something useful, and the piece it uncovered attacks as well.

deeper.title: Danger levels
body: Not every threat is equal. A **check** or a threat of **mate** is more dangerous than a threat to a piece.
So when one of your pieces is attacked, do not rush to save it. First look: do I have a check, or a bigger threat, that Black must answer?

board.caption: Black's rook attacks your knight. Must you move it?

deeper.prompt: Your knight is attacked. Don't save it. Find the check that leads to checkmate in two.
deeper.hint: Which queen check on the back rank forces mate?
deeper.explain: **Qd8+** forces the rook to block on e8, and **Qxe8#** is checkmate. The knight on b5 never matters: a mate threat outranks a threat to a piece.

deeper.prompt: Your knight is attacked by the queen. Don't move it away. Find the better move.
deeper.hint: A check that also attacks something big.
deeper.explain: **Ne7+** gives check and attacks the queen at the same time. Black must answer the check, and then your knight takes the queen.

deeper.prompt: Black attacks your bishop. You can give check, but it wins nothing. What should you do?
options: Look for a reply that wins something, or just save the bishop. A check that wins nothing only helps Black.
Always play the check, because checks come first
Ignore both and push a pawn
deeper.explain: The checklist tells you what to **look at**, not what to play. A check is only worth playing if it leads somewhere. If it does not, save the piece.

deeper.title: Discovered attacks
deeper.intro: Move the front piece and let the one behind it do the damage.

puzzles.hint: Move the knight with check. What does the rook on d1 now attack?
puzzles.explain: **Nf6+** is check, and it uncovers the rook's attack on the queen. After the king deals with the check, **Rxd7** wins her.

puzzles.hint: Capture with check, and see what is uncovered.
puzzles.explain: **Nxf6+** takes a rook with check and uncovers the rook on d1's attack on the other one. After the recapture, **Rxd8+** wins the second rook.

puzzles.hint: You are Black. Take the knight with check, and look at the d-file.
puzzles.explain: **Bxe3+** wins the knight with check and uncovers the rook's attack on the queen. After the king moves, **Rxd1+** wins her.

deeper.title: Danger levels
deeper.intro: One of your pieces is attacked in each of these. Ignore it, and find the move that is more dangerous.

puzzles.hint: Your rook is attacked, but a check comes first.
puzzles.explain: **Qc8+** forces the rook to block on e8, and **Qxe8#** is checkmate. The attack on your rook never matters.

puzzles.hint: Your bishop is attacked twice. Ignore that, and take on f7 with check.
puzzles.explain: **Qxf7+** is protected by the bishop, so the king has to go to h8. Then **Qf8#** is checkmate, because the queen covers the whole back rank. The attacks on your bishop never mattered.

puzzles.hint: You are Black. Your knight is attacked, but check comes first.
puzzles.explain: **Qc1+** forces the rook to block on d1, and **Qxd1#** is checkmate.
